sections.h2: Selling a Granite City house quickly
sections.html:
The quickest routes are an as-is cash purchase or a competitively priced listing, and both run through the same Madison County recording steps. What changes is how many conditions stand between you and closing day.

  • As-is cash sale: no mortgage underwriting, and the buyer normally takes the house with its repairs.
  • Agent listing: wider exposure, but a buyer's lender may require an appraisal and repair requests.
  • For sale by owner: you keep control of price and showings and pay for a contract review yourself.

Granite City has a lot of older, modestly priced housing, so condition often drives the choice. If a roof, furnace or foundation is the sticking point, compare what repairs would cost against a sale to someone who will handle them.

Granite City is one of the lower-priced housing markets in the St. Louis area. Population is 26,807, down from 27,563 in 2020, and the city has 11,562 households.

In the 2020 census, 11.4 percent of the city's housing units were vacant. A house that is clean, secured and priced to the neighborhood competes better against vacant stock. If your house is one of the empty ones, keep the utilities connected, since the city requires them to be on for an occupancy inspection.

Granite City was planned as a company town in 1896 by the Niedringhaus brothers, who made graniteware kitchen utensils and later steel. A street grid with lettered avenues and numbered streets was laid out, with Niedringhaus Avenue as the only exception.

The result is a city of neighborhood pockets: Downtown, East Granite, West Granite, North Granite, the Nameoki Strip, the Bellemore area and the Wilson Park area. Wilson Park is known for turn-of-the-20th-century homes, while East Granite is mostly newer residential subdivisions. Name the neighborhood in your listing, since buyers shop by area.

Granite City sits in the American Bottom beside the Chain of Rocks Canal on the Mississippi, with Horseshoe Lake to the southeast. Interstate 270 crosses the northern edge, and Interstates 255, 70, 55 and 64 pass just south and east. Route 3 runs along the western side and reaches downtown St. Louis over the McKinley Bridge.

The city stayed dry in the Great Flood of 1993 because levees protect it along the river and the canal. Even so, a buyer in this area will usually ask about flood zone status and insurance, so have your elevation or insurance information ready if you have it.

Industry remains central, with steel and food manufacturers among the long-running employers, which keeps steady local demand for housing.

sections.h2: Schools and parks buyers ask about
sections.html:
Granite City Community Unit School District 9 serves the city. It runs five elementary schools (Frohardt, Mitchell, Wilson, Prather and Maryville), Grigsby Intermediate, Coolidge Junior High and Granite City High School. Families also have two Catholic kindergarten through eighth grade schools, Holy Family and St. Elizabeth, and Rivers of Life Christian School.

The Granite City Park District owns 13 parks, and its most notable, Wilson Park, includes a 1.4 mile paved trail, a pool and an ice rink. Horseshoe Lake State Park, retail along the Nameoki Strip and the Madison County Transit bikeways are also worth a line in the listing.

sections.h2: Order of steps for a Granite City sale
sections.html: A simple sequence keeps the city and county pieces from colliding. Call the Building and Zoning Department first and ask whether an Occupancy Permit applies to your sale. If it does, file the application, pay the fee and book an inspection slot with the utilities still on. While that is moving, ask your title company to prepare the deed with the grantee's tax billing address, the parcel number and the PTAX form. A cash buyer can skip the lender's appraisal, but the permit and the recording steps stay the same, so start them as soon as you have a signed contract.

sections.h2: Occupancy permit when a house changes hands
sections.html:
The owner of a home must apply for an Occupancy Permit when occupancy or ownership changes. Call the Building and Zoning Department at (618) 452-6218 to confirm how the rule applies to your sale and your buyer before you set a closing date.

  • The permit must be obtained within 30 days of application.
  • The owner pays the fees and arranges access for the inspection.
  • Utilities must be on for the inspection.
  • Inspection slots run from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, and you can book once the application is in and the fee is paid.

The same office enforces a property maintenance code, and grass on private property must be kept below eight inches.

The Building and Zoning Department asks for 24 hours of advance notice for inspections and takes scheduling calls at (618) 452-6218. Get permits before any home improvement project, which matters if you are tempted to finish a repair before listing.

  • Inspections are required at set stages, such as before concrete is poured, before insulation and drywall, and after the structure is finished and before it is used.
  • New structures cannot be used or occupied until final inspections pass and a certificate of use and occupancy is issued.
  • Grass on private property must stay below eight inches, and below five inches in the right-of-way between the curb and sidewalk.
  • Trash and recycling go to the curb the evening before pickup, no earlier than 6:00 p.m.

Ask the department about permits for any addition, deck or finished basement before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: How the deed is recorded in Madison County
sections.html:
Granite City is in Madison County, so the deed goes to the Madison County Recorder. Every deed needs a grantee name and address for tax billing and a permanent parcel number, along with a return-to name and address and the name and address of the person who prepared it.

  • An Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration (PTAX) or a statement of exemption.
  • A Plat Act affidavit, which must accompany all deeds.
  • Transfer tax at the rates the office prints: $.50 per $500 or part thereof to the state and $.25 per $500 or part thereof to the county.

If you pay by check, the Recorder asks for the recording fee and the transfer tax on separate checks. Your title company usually handles all of this at the closing table.

faqs.q: Does Granite City require an inspection before I can sell?
faqs.a: An owner must apply for an Occupancy Permit when occupancy or ownership changes, so call (618) 452-6218 to see how it applies to your sale. When one is required, the owner pays and the utilities must be on for the inspection.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Granite City house?
faqs.a: At the Madison County Recorder, since Granite City is in Madison County. Bring the deed, a parcel number, the PTAX form or exemption statement and a Plat Act affidavit.

faqs.q: What transfer tax rates apply in Madison County?
faqs.a: The Recorder prints $.50 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration for the State of Illinois and $.25 per $500 or part thereof for the county. Your closing agent calculates the amount from the declaration.

faqs.q: Is Granite City in a flood area?
faqs.a: The city is on the Mississippi River plain and is protected by levees along the river and the Chain of Rocks Canal. It did not flood in 1993, but check the flood zone and insurance details for your own address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Granite City house with tenants or code problems?
faqs.a: Yes. An as-is buyer can take a house with tenants in place or an open maintenance notice. Ask the Building and Zoning Department about any violation before closing so it does not surprise anyone.
